method_card.title: Future Plans and Career Aspirations
method_card.content:
This lesson covers post-16 plans, university and career aspirations using three future structures and Konjunktiv II. The German post-16 education system differs significantly from the UK system — key terms are culturally specific and must be learned accurately.

GermanEnglish
das AbiturGerman school-leaving certificate (≈ A-levels)
die Ausbildungapprenticeship / vocational training
das Studiumuniversity studies / degree course
die Universität (Uni)university
die Fachhochschule (FH)university of applied sciences (≈ polytechnic)
das Praktikumwork experience / internship
der Berufjob / profession
in der Zukunftin the future
nach der Schuleafter school
ich werde ... werdenI will become ...
ich würde gernI would like to (conditional)
ich möchteI would like (polite modal)

Grammar focus 1 — three future structures (all must appear in your writing):

(1) Present tense + future adverb: Nächstes Jahr mache ich ein Praktikum. (Next year I am doing work experience.) Simple, natural, frequently used in spoken German.

(2) Werden + infinitive (formal future): Modal-style structure — werden at position 2, infinitive at the clause end. Ich werde Informatik studieren. (I will study computer science.) In a subordinate clause, both verbs go to the end: weil ich Informatik studieren werde.

(3) Modal + infinitive at end: Ich möchte auf die Universität gehen. or Ich will eine Ausbildung machen.

Grammar focus 2 — Konjunktiv II for aspirations and advice: Use ich würde gern + infinitive for 'I would like to': Ich würde gern Medizin studieren. Use man sollte + infinitive for advice: Man sollte gute Noten bekommen. Use es wäre + adjective for 'it would be': Es wäre toll, wenn ich das Abitur bestehe.

Model paragraph: Nach der Schule möchte ich das Abitur machen und dann werde ich auf die Universität gehen. Ich würde gern Medizin studieren, weil ich Ärztin werden möchte. Ich denke, dass eine Ausbildung auch eine gute Option wäre.
(After school I would like to do my Abitur and then I will go to university. I would like to study Medicine because I would like to become a doctor. I think that an apprenticeship would also be a good option.)
steps: Learn German post-16 vocabulary: Abitur (A-levels equivalent), Ausbildung (apprenticeship), Studium, Universität, Fachhochschule
Drill all three future structures: present + time adverb, werden + infinitive at end, möchte/will + infinitive at end
Use Konjunktiv II: ich würde gern + infinitive, man sollte + infinitive, es wäre + adjective
Build longer plans: nach der Schule + then + future structure + reason with weil + verb at end
Compare German and UK post-16 options (Abitur vs A-levels, Ausbildung vs apprenticeship, FH vs polytechnic)

exam_context.frequency: Higher-yield topic for writing and speaking — future tense and Konjunktiv II are required for top marks

worked_examples.question: Translate to English: 'Ich möchte auf die Universität gehen.'

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: Ich möchte = I would like. This is the conditional form of mögen — used as a polite wish.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: auf die Universität = to university. Note: gehen uses auf + accusative for 'going to' an institution.

steps.label: Step 3
steps.content: gehen = to go. This is the infinitive at the end, after möchte.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: I would like to go to university.

worked_examples.question: Explain the word order rule with werden + infinitive.

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: Werden is conjugated and goes at position 2 in a main clause: Ich werde Informatik studieren.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: The main verb (infinitive) goes to the end of the main clause — just like a modal verb.

steps.label: Step 3
steps.content: In a subordinate clause (after weil, dass, obwohl), both verbs go to the end, conjugated form last: weil ich Informatik studieren werde.

worked_examples.question: What is the difference between 'ich möchte ... gehen' and 'ich werde ... gehen'?

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: Ich möchte auf die Uni gehen uses the modal möchte — it expresses a wish or preference (I would like to go). It is polite and tentative.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: Ich werde auf die Uni gehen uses werden + infinitive — it states a definite plan or fact about the future (I will go).

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: Use möchte for wishes and preferences; use werden + infinitive for firm future plans. Both have the infinitive at the clause end.

bronze.question: Match the German post-16 education words to the English meaning
Match the German future tense phrases to the English meaning
Complete the future plan sentence — möchte + infinitive at end
sentence_parts: Nach der Schule möchte ich auf die Universität

gaps.correct_explain: With möchte, the infinitive gehen goes to the end: Ich möchte auf die Universität gehen.

wrong.gehe: gehe is the conjugated ich form. After möchte, use the infinitive: gehen.
wrong.gegangen: gegangen is the past participle. After möchte, use the infinitive: gehen.

bronze.question: Complete the Konjunktiv II sentence — würde + infinitive at end

gaps.rule: Konjunktiv II — würde + infinitive at end
gaps.correct_explain: With würde, the infinitive studieren goes to the end. Note: no ge- prefix — this is the infinitive, not the past participle.

wrong.studiere: studiere is present tense. With würde gern, use the infinitive: studieren.
wrong.studiert: studiert is conjugated (er/sie) or present tense. After würde, use the infinitive: studieren.

bronze.question: What does 'Ich werde nach dem Abitur eine Ausbildung machen' mean?
options: I will do an apprenticeship after my Abitur
I am doing an apprenticeship before my Abitur
I would like to do an apprenticeship
I did an apprenticeship after school

bronze.question: What does 'Man kann ohne Studium glücklich sein' mean?
options: One can be happy without a university degree
One cannot be happy without studying
You should always study at university

bronze.source_text: Ich möchte in der Zukunft Medizin studieren.
model_answers: I would like to study Medicine in the future.
I would like to study medicine in the future.
hints: in der Zukunft = in the future

silver.question: Complete the sentence (no word bank)
silver.english: My ideal future **would be** exciting and I **would have** good colleagues.

gaps.correct_explain: wäre (would be) is the Konjunktiv II form of sein. It does not need an infinitive at the end.

wrong.ist: ist is present tense. For hypothetical/ideal descriptions, use wäre.

gaps.correct_explain: hätte (would have) is the Konjunktiv II form of haben.

wrong.habe: habe is present tense. For hypothetical descriptions, use hätte.

silver.question: Find and fix the grammatical error
silver.sentence: Ich werde nach dem Abitur studieren Informatik.
silver.error_type: Werden + infinitive — infinitive at clause end
silver.explanation: With werden + infinitive, the infinitive goes to the end of the clause. The object comes between werde and the infinitive: Ich werde Informatik studieren.
silver.translation: I will study computer science after my Abitur.

silver.question: Build the sentence in German
silver.english: I would like to get an apprenticeship after school.

distractor_labels.mache: wrong form — after möchte, you need the infinitive machen, not the conjugated form mache

silver.source_text: On one hand, a university degree is important. On the other hand, an apprenticeship is more practical.
model_answers: Einerseits ist ein Studium wichtig. Andererseits ist eine Ausbildung praktischer.

silver.question: Put these words in the correct order to form a sentence

gold.source_text: After school I will go to university and study Medicine. I would like to become a doctor because I find it interesting to help people. I think that an apprenticeship would also be a good option.
model_answers: Nach der Schule werde ich auf die Universität gehen und Medizin studieren. Ich möchte Ärztin werden, weil ich es interessant finde, Menschen zu helfen. Ich denke, dass eine Ausbildung auch eine gute Option wäre.

Check: werden + infinitive at end (gehen, studieren), möchte + profession + werden (no article), weil + verb at end (finde), infinitive with zu (helfen zu), dass + Konjunktiv II wäre at end of clause, noun capitalisation. Respond in JSON: {"quality":"excellent|good|needs_work|not_valid","feedback":"2-3 sentences","improvement":"optional correction"}

gold.question: Build the sentence in German
gold.english: I would say that a university degree is important.

distractor_labels.sage: wrong tense — sage is present tense. The conditional requires würde + sagen (infinitive at end of main clause).
distractor_labels.sein: wrong form — in the dass clause, the verb must be conjugated: ist (not the infinitive sein)

gold.question: Role Play
gold.scenario: You are at a leisure centre and get talking to the receptionist about your studies and future plans.

bullets.prompt: Say what you plan to do after school and give a reason.
bullets.model_answer: Nach der Schule werde ich das Abitur machen und dann möchte ich auf die Universität gehen, weil ich Ingenieurin werden möchte.
bullets.note: werden + infinitive at end, möchte + gehen (infinitive at end), weil + modal at end in subordinate clause

bullets.prompt: Describe what you would like to study and say what it would be like.
bullets.model_answer: Ich würde gern Naturwissenschaften studieren. Es wäre sehr interessant und ich würde viel über die Welt lernen.
bullets.note: würde gern + infinitive at end, es wäre + adjective, würde + infinitive at end

bullets.prompt: Ask if the leisure centre offers any student discount.
bullets.model_answer: Haben Sie einen Rabatt für Studenten?
bullets.note: formal Sie register — leisure centre is a prescribed transactional setting, polite question

bullets.prompt: Say what you will do at university in your free time.
bullets.model_answer: In meiner Freizeit werde ich schwimmen und Sport treiben.
bullets.note: werden + infinitive at end, inversion after time phrase (in meiner Freizeit)

gold.question: Write 40-50 words in German about your future plans and career aspirations. Include: what you plan to do after school and why, whether you prefer university or an apprenticeship, what job you would like to do, and one piece of advice for someone making these choices.
gold.ai_system_prompt: You are a GCSE German examiner marking extended writing about future plans and career aspirations. Mark on: Communication (post-school plan, university vs Ausbildung, job aspiration, advice), Range of language (all three future structures: present + adverb, werden + infinitive, möchte/will + infinitive; Konjunktiv II: würde gern, wäre, sollte; weil/dass/obwohl + verb-final; discourse markers), Accuracy (werden + infinitive at end, Konjunktiv II forms, profession without article after werden/sein, verb-final in subordinate clauses, noun capitalisation, umlauts). Be encouraging. Respond in JSON: {"quality":"excellent|good|needs_work|not_valid","feedback":"3-4 sentences covering each criterion","improvement":"One specific grammar point to work on"}

gold.question: Listen and type what you hear
gold.audio_text: Ich würde sagen, dass das Studium wichtig ist, weil man viel lernt. Jedoch möchte ich zuerst eine Ausbildung machen.
gold.correct_text: Ich würde sagen, dass das Studium wichtig ist, weil man viel lernt. Jedoch möchte ich zuerst eine Ausbildung machen.
gold.translation: I would say that university is important because you learn a lot. However, I would like to do an apprenticeship first.

gold.question: Find and fix the grammatical error (Higher — Konjunktiv II in dass clause)
gold.sentence: Ich würde sagen, dass das Abitur wichtig sein.
gold.explanation: In a dass clause, the verb must be conjugated, not in the infinitive. Das Abitur is singular, so use ist (or wäre for conditional): dass das Abitur wichtig ist.
gold.translation: I would say that the Abitur is important.
